Task: fix the issues found by the FIRST RENDERED Impeccable critique of the reader and reply/compose UI of Email OS (Vue 3 + Tauri desktop email client, Operate-mode app UI). This branch is stacked on PR #35 (branch impeccable/reader-compose-critique-2, https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/35), which is not merged yet; open ONE PR for this work with base = impeccable/reader-compose-critique-2 (retarget to main once #35 merges; if #35 has already merged, rebase on origin/main and target main). The repo remote is an internal proxy that `gh` does not recognise: use `gh pr create --repo BbrSofiane/email-os ...`.

READ FIRST (fully): PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md (esp. Layout geometry > Reader, Parity gaps 17 and 18, Composer, Inputs / Fields, Reader Message Disclosures, Typography > Reading), and the critique that produced this task: /home/exedev/.t3/worktrees/email-os/impeccable-reader-compose-critique-2/.impeccable/critique/2026-11-09T20-01-29Z__src-components-readerview-vue.md (uncommitted in the other worktree, read it by that absolute path; it is the archive of the report below). Also read the Impeccable skill refs at ~/.claude/skills/impeccable/reference/{polish,layout,clarify}.md and craft-floor.md (read craft-floor immediately before editing UI), and the repo's `implement` skill / persona-feature-engineer agent (.claude/skills/implement, .claude/agents/persona-feature-engineer.md): use it for implementation, test-first (failing test, then fix). Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` if node_modules is missing. Checks: `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm exec vite build`, `~/.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable detect --json <touched .vue files>` (style.css has 6 known pre-existing advisories; ignore 'CONTEXT_STALE' notes, do not repair them). Baseline on the parent branch: 1162 tests passed / 34 skipped (4 opt-in Chrome suites).

NEW CAPABILITY vs the previous pass: a real browser exists here through the T3 preview tools (deferred; load with ToolSearch `select:mcp__t3-code__preview_open,mcp__t3-code__preview_snapshot,mcp__t3-code__preview_act,mcp__t3-code__preview_evaluate,mcp__t3-code__preview_resize,mcp__t3-code__t3_preview_close`). Start the fixture-only preview with `pnpm exec vite --port 5199 --strictPort --host 127.0.0.1` in the background, open your own tab, and MEASURE before and after each fix (getBoundingClientRect / getComputedStyle / document.activeElement) at 1280x800, 1000x700 and documentElement font-size 20px. The preview page adds a ~55px synthetic-workspace banner, so absolute y values include it. Stop the dev server and close your tab at the end. Synthetic data only; there is no Send in this product and no real provider writes.

ISSUES TO FIX (from the rendered critique, 29/40; owner decisions already made: fix both P1s, keep the thread visible while replying, fix the CODE to meet the DESIGN.md claims rather than rewording them):
1. [P1] Saving an attachment drops keyboard focus to <body>. In src/components/MessageAttachments.vue the Save button is swapped for `Saving…` + `Cancel`; pressing Enter on Save moved document.activeElement to BODY. Retry (same file) already has a focus-safe pattern (button stays mounted with aria-disabled, group takes focus on success): apply the same idea to Save/Saving…/Cancel so focus never falls to body, including when the transfer finishes or fails and when Cancel is used. The AttachmentChooser has the same Save button swap: check and fix it if it has the same flaw (it is a modal with its own focus trap). No new live regions (the status line stays quiet; saved/failed lines keep role=status / role=alert as they are). Also: the active message's toggle has no focus ring of its own (the 3px active bar is the only cue, so a keyboard user cannot tell active from focused). Propose and implement the smallest cue that keeps the One Signal Rule (e.g. a non-lavender focus treatment or a ring only when :focus-visible), measure it, and document it.
2. [P1] The loading skeleton still jumps. Row pitch (49px) is right, but with a known row identity the first skeleton row starts ~56px lower than the first real message (measured y=244.3 vs 187.9 on a replica) because the `Loading conversation…` status line and the sender/date identity line push the rows down. DESIGN.md says the pane does not jump; make that true. Fold the status into the identity line or reserve the exact height with the loaded layout's margins; keep `Loading conversation…` text and role=status exactly (tests pin them), keep aria-hidden skeleton, keep J/K navigation smooth with no empty frame (tests/reader-navigation.smooth.test.ts). The fixture loads instantly, so to measure a REAL load you will need to slow it (e.g. delay the fixture client's getConversation via a query flag or temporary local patch that you do NOT commit, or inject the same markup into the live reader as the critique did, but prefer a real delayed load) and compare the first-skeleton-row y with the first-real-message y; add a test that pins the structure you choose.
3. [P2] The docked reply composer covers the message it answers. With Cc/Subject open the thread scroller is 241px at 1280x800 (225px at a 20px root); the message being replied to is hidden behind its own composer (its quote sits inside the card). Keep the latest message visible: e.g. when the composer opens, scroll the replied-to (latest) message into view above the card and/or cap the card so a minimum thread strip always remains (keep `max-height: 60%` text in ReplyComposer.vue because tests grep it, or update those tests if you change the cap deliberately). Measure at 1280x800, 1000x700 and 20px root; the answered message must be visible and keyboard focus/scroll positions must stay sane.
4. [P2] The contact pane shifts while a reply is open: a 'Composing to Ada Fixture / ada@example.test' line is inserted at the top of ContactPane (y=55 to 87), moving the contact name from y=87 to 120 and the email from 143 to 176, breaking DESIGN.md's rule (name on the tab line, email on the first-list line). Remove the line or move it below the thread list so the pinned lines never move; update ContactPane tests and DESIGN.md accordingly.
5. [P2] Details values are ragged: `.message-field-label` has no fixed width, so From/To/Cc/Sent values start at x=126/109/111/124 while Details itself is at x=90. Give the label a fixed width (about 3rem, on-scale) or use a two-column grid so values share one x.
6. [P2] Composer geometry: the reply composer's inner padding is 10px but the docked new-message card's is 16px; the undocked new-message card is 613px tall (139 to 752) with the footer at y=382 and ~360px of dead space (size it to content or pin sensibly); the attachment chooser's file list is indented 40px (x=328 vs 288 for the text above it, scoped style in AttachmentChooser.vue). One shared padding value; zero the chooser list indent.
7. [P3] Identical clock glyphs: 'Remind me on this device' (reader header) and 'Reminders' (app header) are the same SVG; and two controls are both named 'Reply' (header glyph and the per-message glyph; run 1 noted the per-message one could go, but removing a visible control is a separate decision: do NOT remove it, just make the accessible names/titles distinguishable if that can be done tersely, e.g. keep 'Reply' on the header glyph and 'Reply to latest message' wording only if it does not break tests/R-hint conventions; otherwise leave and report).
Minor, only if trivial and safe: the `Show quoted text`/`Save` ghost buttons place their text 8px inside the 90px text edge (the 8px button padding) — consider aligning the text to the inset with a negative margin like `.selection-actions`; the Esc hint beside `Save and close` is bare text; signature and quote share one style (leave).

CONSTRAINTS / OUT OF SCOPE: honour PRODUCT.md 'Standing constraints' (safe literal plain text, no HTML rendering of message content, no auto-open of attachments, drafts local-only, no Send, no optimistic UI). DRAFT INTEGRITY stays deferred: do not change draft creation/dedupe/cleanup (R then Esc leaving blank drafts, resuming drafts, a Draft marker in the reader status line). Do not touch the drawer panels (DraftsPanel, ActivityPanel, RemindersPanel, CachedTrashPanel; DraftsPanel embeds DraftEditorCore, so keep its API compatible and edits minimal), AccountPanel/ProviderDestinations/first-run, search, the bulk selection bar or notice dock (another thread may be touching them; branch impeccable/drawer-panels and impeccable/account-first-run exist). Do not change the Rust DTO/wire format. Keep editable/IME shortcut protection, announcements (keep every live region quiet), focus handling, reduced-motion and J/K smoothness intact. Voice: terse, factual, sentence-case, no exclamation marks. Tokens only (no hardcoded colours), on-scale spacing and radii, :focus-visible on every new interactive element.

DOCS: update DESIGN.md wherever a claim changes or is newly verified (Layout geometry > Reader, gap 17/18, Composer, ContactPane), and add a short run-4 note in a new file under .impeccable/critique/ in the existing format (see the 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-09 files there on the parent branch) with before/after MEASURED numbers.

DONE MEANS: commits per logical fix on this branch with clear messages (end each commit message with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`; end the PR body with `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`), all checks green, the PR opened and linked to this thread, and a final report stating per issue: what changed, the before/after measurements from the real browser, what you rejected or could not verify, and anything deferred.

# Product

## Register

product

## Users

Initially a single person: the author, dogfooding a single-account desktop client (macOS first) against their own Gmail inbox in focused, keyboard-first sessions. They move through a high volume of mail quickly, want to reach "done" on each conversation, and need to trust that every action (archive, bulk processing, undo, send) did exactly what it claimed. The provider's own client remains the fallback.

Longer term: technically capable people who want to compose their own email workflow (custom views, triage signals, commands, automations), manually or with an agent, without rebuilding sync, credentials, or send safety.

The primary task on most screens is triage: scan the list, open a conversation, decide, act, move on.

## Product Purpose

A composable email client: a trusted mail engine (sync, safe rendering, credentials, action execution) with replaceable signals, views, commands, and workflows on top. It ships an opinionated reference experience, a compact Superhuman-style browsing and keyboard flow, rather than a blank toolkit.

The near-term goal is a complete, trustworthy inbox-processing session. Strategic scope is set by `docs/adr/0001-single-account-desktop-email-client.md` and `superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md`; this file does not expand it.

Success looks like: the author processes their inbox faster and with more confidence than in their previous client, and every automated or bulk action is previewable, reported honestly (including partial success and "outcome unknown"), and undoable where undo is real.

## Brand Personality

**Focused, precise, trustworthy.**

- **Focused:** the interface recedes so the mail and the next decision are what's on screen. Dense, quiet, few competing elements.
- **Precise:** exact states, exact counts, exact wording. No vague "something went wrong", no rounded-off truth about what happened.
- **Trustworthy:** the client never overstates what it did. Pending, failed, partial, and ambiguous outcomes are visible and distinct. Automation shows its work before it acts.

Voice is terse and factual: short labels, plain verbs, no exclamation marks, no cheerleading.

## Anti-references

- **Gmail-web clutter:** toolbars of rarely-used icons, chrome competing with content, permanent competing panels.
- **"AI magic" email products:** AI destinations, sparkle icons, generated summaries presented as fact, fabricated contact enrichment, automation that acts without a preview.
- **Superhuman feature-parity clone:** Superhuman is the visual and interaction reference for browsing (layout, density, type, keyboard feel), and close look parity there is a goal. Features and workflows are our own; don't import Superhuman's product scope or claim verified behavioral parity.
- **Generic SaaS dashboard aesthetics:** card stacks and grids, gradient heroes, oversized rounded panels, decorative illustration or motion.
- **Optimistic UI that lies:** "Done" before the provider confirmed, silent retries of ambiguous sends, dead controls that look actionable.

## Design Principles

1. **Honest state over smooth feel.** When speed and truthfulness conflict, show the truth. Every action has a visible pending, success, partial, failed, or unknown state. Show evidence and coverage, including unknown and retained facts.
2. **Keyboard first, mouse welcome.** Every core triage path is reachable and discoverable from the keyboard; pointer interaction is supported, never required.
3. **Content is the interface.** Chrome stays quiet and compact so the list and the conversation dominate. Add UI only when it earns its space in the triage loop; reuse established commands, navigation and recovery surfaces before adding new ones.
4. **Preview before power.** Bulk actions, automations, and agent-proposed changes show what they will do before they do it, and report exactly what they did after. Focus, bulk selection and message identity stay separate concepts.
5. **Opinionated defaults, replaceable parts.** Ship one strong way of working; design surfaces so views, signals, and commands can be swapped without breaking the core experience.

Standing constraints: ordinary reading stays local and non-mutating; message content renders as safe literal plain text; drafts stay local-only.

## Accessibility & Inclusion

Not a formal priority at this stage; no WCAG conformance target or certification is implied. Keyboard operability and visible focus remain required because they are core to the keyboard-first model. Don't regress behavior that already exists (explicit action labels, editable/IME shortcut protection, reduced-motion alternatives, selection/outcome announcements). The existing desktop/contact breakpoints remain authoritative; no new mobile UI. Revisit if the audience expands beyond the author.

# Craft floor

Load this after the direction is settled, and build without announcing the checklist. A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here except a line marked as a ban; your own habit does not. When the design hook is active it already enforces the mechanical checks below as you edit: act on its findings instead of re-auditing each rule.

## Verify

Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in each batched look at the render, not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.

- **Contrast:** body and placeholder text ≥4.5:1, large text ≥3:1. On colored surfaces tint secondary text from that hue or the foreground; never gray.
- **Depth:** shadows carry an offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset colored halo is decoration.
- **Spacing:** tight groups, generous separation, more space above a heading than below it. Read the computed values.
- **Type:** body measure 65–75ch, display max 6rem, tracking floor -0.04em, balanced headings, obvious scale and weight steps. Run the real copy at every breakpoint and fix what overflows.
- **Motion:** one authored moment, not scattered effects and not one identical entrance on every section. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default. Reach past transform and opacity: blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, and shadow belong to the palette when they stay smooth.
- **States:** hover, disabled, loading, error, empty. Plus real content, working controls, responsive composition, keyboard focus.
- **Browser surfaces:** the parts you did not draw still carry the design. Text selection, the caret, custom scrollbars, focus rings, underline offset, and the numerals in tabular data all ship with browser defaults that belong to no design system. Theme them from the palette. This is the cheapest signal that a page was built rather than assembled, and the one models skip most reliably.
- **Copy:** the product's own language. Controls name their action; errors name the problem and the recovery.
- **Coverage:** every brief requirement present and findable within seconds.

## Refuse

These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.

Page scaffolds:

- Same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text as the page structure. Cards are the lazy container; nested cards are always wrong.
- The hero-metric template: big number, small label, supporting stats, accent.
- A kicker or eyebrow above a heading. This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.
- Section numbers (01 / 02 / 03) unless the sequence itself carries information the reader needs.
- A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus.

Surface habits:

- Gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.
- Glass and blur as decoration rather than as a specific effect.
- A colored `border-left` or `border-right` above 1px on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts.
- Hard offset shadows (`box-shadow: 4px 4px 0`) outside a world that is actually neobrutalist. The zero-blur block shadow is a costume, not a depth system; a world that did not choose it never earns it as a default.
- Sparklines, progress rings, and soft-shadowed rounded rectangles standing in for content.
- Monospace as a costume for "technical" rather than for code, data, or measurement.
- A system display face (Impact, Arial Black, the platform sans) as the display voice of an own-world page. Source and self-host a face whose character matches the approved lettering; the closest installed font is a failure, not a fallback.
- Unicode glyphs or emoji standing in for an icon system. Icons are drawn, from a real library or authored SVG, in one consistent stroke and weight.
- Geometric masks standing in for organic contours. A circle, polygon, or radial-gradient cutout approximating a photographic subject's edge is the cheap version of the effect and reads worse than omitting it. Derive an alpha matte from the actual image, or produce a cut-out asset.
- Light or dark picked by category. Pick it from the use scene: who, where, under what ambient light.

The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.

> **Additional context needed**: quality bar and shipping constraints.

Polish is refinement, never concealed redesign. Preserve the incumbent visual world, content, behavior, and everything outside scope. If the concept itself is wrong, say so and recommend redesign or `bolder` instead of smuggling in a replacement.

A detector result is defect evidence, not proof of quality. Inspect the rendered experience and real interaction path.

## 1. Establish the system

Read DESIGN.md and representative tokens, shared components, patterns, and neighboring flows. If no formal system exists, use coherent project conventions.

Classify each drift before fixing it:

- **missing token:** the system needs a reusable value;
- **one-off implementation:** an existing shared component or pattern should replace it;
- **conceptual mismatch:** the flow, information architecture, or hierarchy differs from comparable product areas;
- **local defect:** the implementation is simply incomplete or inconsistent.

Fix the cause at the narrowest correct level. Ask when a binding system principle cannot be inferred.

## 2. Gather the evidence

Use the feature yourself at the surface's representative sizes: desktop and mobile on the web; on a native platform (`ios` / `android` / `adaptive`), the shipped device classes on the simulator, emulator, or hardware, captured per the platform reference's Verifying the build section. Determine:

- whether the path is functionally complete;
- the intended quality bar and time available;
- known constraints or deliberately unfinished work;
- the states, content lengths, roles, and input methods users will actually encounter.

If a prior critique exists, use it as one input:

```bash
.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable critique-storage latest "<resolved target>" --json
```

Exit 0 returns JSON with the latest snapshot's `body` and an exact `snapshot_file` identity. Retain `snapshot_file` until the end of the pass. For a local file target, the helper compares the file's exact current content fingerprint with the fingerprint captured by critique. Unchanged staged, unstaged, or untracked content remains current; any byte change, deletion, or replacement with a non-file closes the backlog it identified while preserving its trend history and exits 2. A URL target has no local fingerprint and remains current until explicitly closed. When current, incorporate relevant P0/P1 findings from `body` and name the snapshot read. Exit 2 means none exists or the target changed. Perform an independent pass either way.

## 3. Triage

Separate functional defects from cosmetic ones and fix in this order:

1. broken or blocked tasks, data loss, misleading state, and inaccessible paths;
2. missing loading, empty, error, success, disabled, and permission states;
3. flow, hierarchy, responsive, and design-system drift;
4. visual and motion inconsistencies;
5. code and asset cleanup.

Do not perfect one corner while leaving the rest below the same quality bar.

## 4. Polish the whole path

### Flow and hierarchy

- Match neighboring mental models, terminology, disclosure, routing, save behavior, and optimistic or pessimistic patterns.
- Make the primary task and current state obvious without flattening every element to equal weight.
- Ensure arrival, transition, empty, and recovery paths connect instead of behaving as isolated screens.

### Layout and type

- Align to the project's grid and spacing scale; fix optical as well as mathematical alignment.
- Group related content tightly and separate distinct groups generously.

# Implement

Implement the requested change in Email OS. The request can be a task description, an approved plan, or a path to a repository document with a specific item to implement. No ticket service is required.

Usage: `/skill:implement <task description or document path and item>`

All repository paths below are relative to the repository root. The local persona definition is `.pi/agents/persona-feature-engineer.md` from the repository root. Runtimes that mirror these documents through symlinks keep this path authoritative; follow the target, not the mirror location.

## 1. Establish the task

- Read the request and referenced documents. Identify the goal, acceptance criteria, non-goals, and affected code.
- If the request names a broad document, ask which item to implement. Do not treat every proposed feature in that document as approved work.
- Ask for clarification if a product, architecture, data migration, or scope decision is missing. Do not invent requirements.
- Inspect the working-tree status. Preserve pre-existing edits and keep one writer per checkout.

## 2. Gather repository context

Use local code and documentation, not external wiki or code-graph services:

- `README.md` for the project entry points and document map.
- `docs/development.md` for setup, commands, profile isolation, and validation gates.
- `docs/adr/0001-single-account-desktop-email-client.md` for accepted first-build scope.
- The relevant slice or UX contract under `docs/`, and the relevant section of `docs/superhuman-browsing-implementation-plan.md` or `superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md` for browsing work.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` only as a proposal, not as an inventory of implemented behavior. The PRD and older research do not authorize scope expansion.
- Current code and tests to confirm actual behavior. Escalate material conflicts between the task, accepted contracts, and implementation.
